summary:
AirSpace Next is a five-stage In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) and closed-loop atmospheric refining system solving two urgent crises: prohibitive deep-space mission costs and severe urban air pollution on Earth. Built on the zero-waste 3C Loop Theory (Capture, Convert, Circulate) by Team 78 and validated using official NASA datasets (OCO-2, EMIT, MOXIE, Magellan, LADEE), it operates as a compact planetary refinery. It captures toxic planetary gases and urban smog, filters abrasive dust and corrosive vapors via electromagnetic and HEPA barriers, isolates pure gases through centrifugation and cryogenic distillation, and synthesizes eleven mission-critical commodities—including 99.6% breathable oxygen, aerospace graphene, Methalox rocket fuel, potable water, and pure iron.
Calibrated against extreme Earth analogs—polluted megacities like Dhaka, New Delhi, and Lahore, plus arid mineral deserts—AirSpace Next delivers transformative global, economic, and humanitarian value. In space, producing consumables locally cuts launch mass and logistics costs by 50%–60%, making NASA’s Artemis Moon-to-Mars missions sustainable. On Earth, acting as an industrial air scrubber, it protects public health and extends life expectancy by removing toxic PM2.5 and carbon, while upcycling emissions into high-value graphene, clean bio-fuels, and fertilizers to drive a lucrative green economy.

AirSpace Next

 Closed-Loop Multi-Planetary Atmospheric Refining and In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) Architecture

1. Core Problems

Expanding permanent human civilization beyond Earth while protecting our home planet’s environment faces four critical bottlenecks:

  • Prohibitive Deep-Space Launch Mass & Cost: Establishing permanent settlements on the Moon, Mars, and Venus is severely hindered by the immense financial expense and rocket payload limits of launching heavy oxygen tanks, potable water, structural materials, and return propellants out of Earth’s gravity well.
  • Lethal Extraterrestrial Atmospheres & Hardware Degradation: Off-world environments are hostile to human life and precision machinery—characterized by Mars’s 95.3% Carbon Dioxide (CO₂) atmosphere and abrasive iron-oxide dust storms, Venus’s corrosive sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) clouds, and electrostatic lunar regolith dust.
  • Severe Urban Air & Carbon Pollution on Earth: Rapidly industrializing megacities—such as Dhaka, New Delhi, and Lahore—suffer from hazardous levels of fine particulate matter (PM2.5/PM10) and toxic carbon emissions, threatening public health, reducing life expectancy, and wasting valuable carbon feedstocks.
  • Off-World Resource & Energy Scarcity: There is currently no self-sustaining infrastructure to locally manufacture construction materials, grow food, or maintain uninterrupted power during multi-month Martian dust storms and 14-day lunar nights.

2. Operational Framework: The 3C Loop Theory

To solve these challenges, AirSpace Next operates on the 3C Loop Theory (Capture, Convert, Circulate)—a structured, zero-waste engineering framework defined by Team 78 to systematize closed-loop resource recovery:

  • Capture: Draws in toxic planetary atmospheres or urban smog, filters out hazardous particulates, and isolates pure gases (CO₂, CH₄, N₂, Ar) into storage cylinders.
  • Convert: Routes the isolated pure gases and mineral dust into specialized downstream reactors to synthesize eleven mission-critical commodities.
  • Circulate: Supplies the converted resources directly to colony life-support and propulsion systems while looping waste heat and by-products back into the pipeline for continuous, zero-waste operation.

3. How It Works: Five-Stage Atmospheric Refining Pipeline

Operating like a compact extraterrestrial refinery, AirSpace Next processes ambient air through five sequential, automated stages:

  • Stage 1 – Direct Air Intake & Dynamic Pressure Regulation: Variable-speed intake turbines draw in raw ambient air, while internal compressors and automated throttle valves standardize incoming airflow pressure—pressurizing thin atmospheres like Mars (6.1 millibars) upward and stepping down dense atmospheres like Venus (500–1,000 millibars) or Earth (1,013 millibars) to protect internal components.
  • Stage 2 – Multi-Layer Pre-Filtration & Hardware Protection: Incoming air passes through a three-tier barrier where high-intensity electromagnetic coils trap up to 90% of paramagnetic iron-oxide dust, aerospace-grade HEPA filters capture 99.97% of microscopic particles down to 0.3 microns, and activated carbon beds absorb corrosive chemical vapors such as sulfuric acid.
  • Stage 3 – High-Speed Centrifugal Molecular Separation: Purified gas mixtures enter high-speed rotary centrifuges that separate molecules by atomic weight—flinging heavier gases (CO₂, Ar) toward the outer drum walls while concentrating lighter gases (CH₄, N₂, H₂) along the central axis for independent extraction.
  • Stage 4 – Thermal-Pressure Cryogenic Fractional Distillation: Pre-sorted gas streams are compressed and gradually cooled across tiered thermal exchange trays so each gas liquefies at its unique boiling point—isolating pure Argon (-186°C), Oxygen (-183°C), Methane (-161°C), and pressurized CO₂ into dedicated high-pressure cylinders.
  • Stage 5 – Modular Downstream Catalytic Synthesis: Stored pure gases and captured iron-oxide dust are routed into specialized internal reactor modules (such as Solid-Oxide Electrolysis cells and Chemical Vapor Deposition chambers) to synthesize eleven essential resources on demand.

4. Eleven Mission-Critical Commodities & Applications

Using locally harvested feedstocks, AirSpace Next produces eleven vital commodities for space exploration and terrestrial sustainability:

  1. Breathable Pure Oxygen (99.6% Pure O₂): Produced by splitting CO₂ via Solid-Oxide Electrolysis at 800°C; provides continuous breathable air inside astronaut habitats and serves as liquid rocket oxidizer.
  2. Aerospace-Grade Graphene: Synthesized from by-product Carbon Monoxide (CO) inside a Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD) chamber; used to build ultra-lightweight spacecraft hulls, cosmic radiation shields, and high-value industrial electronics on Earth.
  3. High-Impulse Methalox Rocket Propellant: Created by cryogenically liquefying isolated Methane (CH₄) and Oxygen (O₂); enables spacecraft like NASA’s Artemis landers or Starship to refuel on Mars for return journeys to Earth.
  4. Regenerative Fuel-Cell Electricity: Generated by oxidizing Carbon Monoxide and Oxygen inside Solid-Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFC); delivers uninterrupted 24/7 baseload power during global Martian dust storms and 14-day lunar nights when solar power is unavailable.
  5. Potable Water (H₂O): Extracted by thermally cracking sulfuric acid aerosols (H₂SO₄) at 850°C in Venus’s upper cloud layer; supplies clean drinking water and hydroponic irrigation for floating cloud habitats.
  6. Waterless Sulfur Concrete: Formulated by blending molten elemental sulfur (derived from SO₂) with local planetary regolith; constructs radiation-shielded habitats, domes, and rocket landing pads stronger than Portland cement without using a single drop of water.
  7. Cryogenic Coolants & Non-Toxic Fire Suppressants: Liquid Argon (-186°C) cools onboard supercomputers and quantum sensors, while high-pressure CO₂ acts as a safe, non-toxic fire-suppression agent inside crewed modules.
  8. Nitrogen Fertilizers for Space Agriculture: Synthesized via the Haber-Bosch process from captured Nitrogen and Hydrogen to produce ammonia and liquid nitrates; sustains closed-loop hydroponic crop production in off-world greenhouses.
  9. 3D-Printing Space Polymers & Bioplastics: Produced via Fischer-Tropsch synthesis from Carbon Monoxide and recycled Hydrogen to create polyethylene filament; allows astronauts to 3D-print replacement tools, valves, and spare parts on demand.
  10. Pure Metallic Iron (Fe): Extracted by reducing captured iron-oxide dust (Fe₂O₃) with Carbon Monoxide at 750°C; enables local manufacturing of heavy structural beams, fasteners, piping, and tools on Mars and the Moon.
  11. Self-Regenerating Activated Carbon Media: Produced by thermally activating excess solid carbon with CO₂ at 850°C; continuously replenishes Stage 2 chemical scrubbers, eliminating the need for replacement filter shipments from Earth.

5. Key Benefits & Global Impact

AirSpace Next bridges space exploration and environmental engineering as a transformative dual-use technology:

  • 50% to 60% Reduction in Space Launch Mass & Logistics Costs: Producing oxygen, water, propellant, and building materials locally cuts Earth-to-space payload mass and mission costs by 50%–60%, making NASA’s Artemis Moon-to-Mars missions economically viable.
  • Urban Air Purification & Public Health Protection: Validated using NASA OCO-2 and EMIT satellite datasets, deploying AirSpace Next as an industrial air scrubber in heavily polluted megacities like Dhaka, New Delhi, and Lahore removes hazardous PM2.5 and carbon emissions—directly protecting public health and increasing human life expectancy.
  • Green Economy & Carbon-to-Resource Industrialization: Transforms toxic urban smog into high-value commercial products—including industrial graphene, clean bio-Methalox fuel, and agricultural fertilizers—creating a sustainable circular economy on Earth.
  • Long-Term Autonomy & Operational Resilience: With self-regenerating filter media and modular compatibility with nuclear fission power (such as NASA’s Kilopower), the system operates autonomously for years with minimal maintenance.
